plan.p0: Perimeter-ray hypothesis: treat the 9s as two horizontal boundary fragments and side marks of one rectangular figure. Replace missing cells between aligned 9s with 8, then extend those openings vertically or horizontally to the nearest grid edge. Distinguishing assumption: rays are unobstructed and edge-directed; extra objects would not necessarily stop them.
plan.p1: Interior-pipe hypothesis: interpret the 9 pattern as walls of a pipe or frame. Color the enclosed missing portions and only the connected openings leading outward with 8, preserving all non-background cells. Distinguishing assumption: connectivity controls propagation, so an obstacle or disconnected gap would stop the fill.
plan.p2: Symmetry/template hypothesis: regard the 9 arrangement as a partial rectangular motif, complete its implied horizontal and vertical repetitions using 8, and preserve the 9 scaffold. Distinguishing assumption: continuation follows geometric symmetry or periodic structure rather than literal ray visibility, producing different results for asymmetric placements.
plan.p3: Pair-linking hypothesis: identify separated 9 runs or aligned 9 endpoints, fill the direct axis-aligned gaps between each selected pair with 8, and optionally continue an aligned link to an edge. Distinguishing assumption: links are chosen locally by endpoint pairing, not from the global bounding box; ambiguous pairings could therefore yield different fills.
